matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When moving a matchstick, keep its original orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal); sticks cannot be rotated.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before relocating a stick, note its orientation and ensure the destination uses the same orientation.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from an I and placing it as a diagonal in a V, creating an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick may be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Track the stick you take and make sure you add it to another character, keeping the total stick count unchanged.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from a V to turn it into I without adding that diagonal to another symbol.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, every symbol must still be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a valid operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Check each character after the move to confirm it matches a known numeral or operator shape.
matchstick.example: Leaving a V with only one diagonal, which is not a recognized Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Convert the Roman numerals on both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers and ensure the equality holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After finding a candidate stick move, compute the numeric values to confirm the equation is true.
matchstick.example: Changing IV to IX but forgetting to recalculate, resulting in a false equality.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V each consist of exactly two diagonal sticks; after moving a stick, each must still contain two diagonals forming a valid shape.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When relocating a diagonal from a V or X, ensure the remaining diagonal and the moved one together still form a proper V or X.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from V without repositioning it, leaving a single diagonal.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must end with a line exactly matching 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>'.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After solving, output the answer line in the required format, with uppercase letters and collapsed whitespace.
matchstick.example: Omitting the required line or using a different phrasing, causing the answer to be ignored.

matchstick.title: Do not break I
matchstick.principle: When moving the only stick from an I (a single vertical stick), the I character must be removed entirely; you cannot leave a half‑I.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If you take the vertical stick from an I, delete the I symbol from the equation.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from I and leaving a stray placeholder that is not a valid character.

matchstick.title: Diagonal stick reposition for V↔X
matchstick.principle: When a V or X appears, you can change it to the other by moving one of its diagonal sticks to a new location, preserving diagonal orientation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation can be balanced by converting a V to X (or X to V), reposition a diagonal stick accordingly.
matchstick.example: Attempting to turn V into X by removing a diagonal without placing it, leaving an invalid V.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer from I to V/X to create VI or XI
matchstick.principle: If the equation can be balanced by adding an I after a V or X, move a vertical stick from an existing I to that numeral, forming VI or XI.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a V or X needs an extra I to become a valid numeral that balances the equation.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from I to V but leaving the original I unchanged, resulting in an extra stick.

matchstick.title: Preserve exactly one equals sign
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, the equation must still contain exactly one '=' operator; you cannot remove it or turn it into another operator without replacing it elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before finalizing a move, verify that a single '=' remains in the equation.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from the '=' sign to a minus sign, leaving the equation without any '='.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the visual stick move and forgets to check the numeric result.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each candidate transformation, convert both sides to Arabic numbers and confirm the equality.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model omits or mis‑phrases the required final line.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always end the response with the exact line 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>'.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats the operation as removal rather than relocation of a stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Track the stick you take and ensure you place it onto another character.

matchstick.description: Breaking a numeral by moving a stick away, leaving an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model ignores the structural composition of Roman numerals.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After moving a stick, verify that each numeral still matches its standard stick pattern.

matchstick.description: Creating invalid Roman numeral (e.g., IIII, invalid ordering)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats characters as arbitrary stick collections without respecting numeral rules.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check that each resulting numeral follows standard Roman numeral syntax (no four repeats, correct subtractive forms).
